# KDBX test fixtures

## `blank_database.kdbx`

A real KeePass database, used by the KDBX reader tests (P2-T4).

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Source | the blank database that ships with [pykeepass](https://pypi.org/project/pykeepass/) 4.2.0 (`pykeepass/blank_database.kdbx`), MIT licensed |
| Generated by | KeePassXC, as the `<Generator>` element of the decrypted XML says |
| Size | 1365 bytes |
| SHA-256 | `9a6e2380fa0a79534025c0891ebb1b6e06ef2c73c79f661a1d9ab49e436ec7af` |
| Format | KDBX 4.0, AES-256-CBC, GZip, Argon2d (14 rounds, 64 MiB, 2 lanes) |
| Master password | `password` (it is a public test fixture; the file holds no entries and no secrets) |

**Why a real file and not one we wrote:** a parser tested against bytes it produced
itself only proves that it agrees with itself. The KDBX format has at least two places
where a plausible-looking implementation silently disagrees with the format (the version
number, and the width of a header field's length), and both of those were found here by
comparing against a file somebody else wrote.

The expected values in the test are the ones the *reference implementation* produces for
this file, not the ones this project produces: the decrypted XML is compared against
what pykeepass extracts, so the test compares two independent implementations.
